description: Architectural v3: same documented envelope anchors, inferred tapered crown, 2.4 m lens, recessed entrance and operator-plan-informed upper amenities.
floor_count_evidence: R01 p43: 40 floors above ground; model indexing and omitted mezzanine inferred
module_evidence: R01 p43: typical office floor-to-floor 4.15 m; exceptional floors remain inferred
floor_schedule_note: Slab undersides. Ground/double-height lobby and upper exceptional intervals inferred. Interior adds 0.16 m slab + 0.18 m raised construction; highest finished floor = 167.1 m (R01). Model index L01 is ground; index-to-published-level correspondence is approximate.
profile_evidence: R01 max diameter 56.15 m, dome diameter 30 m and rise 22 m. Crown squared radius is 225(1-t)(1+0.25t), t=(z-157.8)/22; its taper, all other connecting knots and datum associations are reconstruction assumptions.
profile_interpolation: shape-preserving cubic Hermite interpolation of squared radius; take nonnegative square root
rotation_evidence: R01 p38 supports the 5-degree floor progression. Our interpolation between model levels and the ground orientation remain assumptions.
unnotched_floor_rule: Use full_floor_levels in this preset. Its closure schedule and minimum atrium inner radius are inferred visualization choices, not a recovered fire-compartment design.
diagrid_topology_evidence: Original computational implementation of the repeating-frame reconstruction relationship discussed in S7-S8.
glazing_grid_evidence: Our computational sampling choice. NOT an interpretation of a Revit 72x72 half-surface grid as whole-building panel counts.
visual_defaults_evidence: Notch dimensions, floor inset, full-floor closure schedule, glazing samples and transparency remain explicit assumptions; six fingers and 5 degree progression supported by R01.
count_note: Counts belong to this procedural preset, not surveyed physical components.
diagrid_evidence: R01 sourced end-zone CHS diameters and walls; architectural builder replaces solid proxies with hollow sections. Intermediate diameters and thicknesses interpolate; not a structural design.
